unconditional_theorems.scope: Infinite input projections contained in O_K,S, for every number field K and finite S. The coordinate bounds also allow open conditions and finite alternatives. Individual-degree bounds concern essential coordinates of a single defining polynomial.
unconditional_theorems.three_coordinate_system_theorem: The equations must have a common irreducible factor of total degree at least four.
unconditional_theorems.nonnegative_scope: Globally nonnegative at one real embedding; includes all sums of squares. This does not exclude sign-changing quartics in three or four coordinates.
unconditional_theorems.three_coordinate_quartic_constraints: Absolutely irreducible, dense smooth rational points, and sign-changing.

unconditional_theorems.scope: s equations of degree at most d over a fixed number field

unconditional_theorems.statement: For fixed r and all nonzero integer labels, the sum of canonical heights of the specified elliptic multiples is bounded linearly by the height of the trace of the sum of their abscissas.
unconditional_theorems.product_version: The analogous trace-of-product bound holds for odd labels.
unconditional_theorems.number_field_scope: The stated conjugate curves must identify with one fixed elliptic curve, and their source points must be pairwise independent over its endomorphism ring modulo torsion.
unconditional_theorems.primary_reference: J. Von Buhren, JTNB 29 (2017), 307-320, Theorem 1.1, doi:10.5802/jtnb.981

unconditional_theorems.scope: Every quadratic extension K=F(sqrt(d)) of every number field F; choose a fixed noncube kappa in F.

zero_inclusive_alternative_with_quantifi.purpose: preserves degree four in the quantified root

unconditional_theorems.product_predicate_general_scope: Every field F of characteristic different from two and every nonsquare d; choose any nonsquare c, for example c=d. No noncube assumption is needed.

unconditional_theorems.scope: All square inputs in every quadratic extension K/F of number fields; two F-input components and one F-auxiliary variable.
unconditional_theorems.height_optimality_scope: Primitive normalization of integral linear multipliers (aU+bV)+(cU+eV)*sqrt(2), with a,b,c,e integers.

unconditional_theorems.scope: Integral E_D:y^2=x^3-D*x over Q(sqrt(2)), P of infinite order, all nonzero integer n_i, with abscissas positive in both embeddings.
unconditional_theorems.number_field_extension: Totally real fields unramified at every odd rational prime, under the same integral and positivity hypotheses.

unconditional_theorems.scope: For every number field F, no rational function A/B of two variables with max(deg A,deg B)<=3 is finite-to-one on the F-points of any nonempty archimedean open set. Some fiber there is infinite with unbounded height.
unconditional_theorems.sharp_example: U^4-delta*V^4 for delta in F not a fourth power has finite F-fibers.
unconditional_theorems.scope_limit: Ambient pairs only; not a lower bound on the coordinates of a Diophantine definition or on measurements of restricted elliptic multiples.

unconditional_theorems.general_scope: Integral Weierstrass model over a totally real field, point Q of infinite order, pairwise coprime nonzero indices, all abscissas positive at all real embeddings.
unconditional_theorems.specified_curve_inequality: loss <= min(v_2(r),3)*log(2); zero if one index is even; for two coprime indices loss <=log(2)
unconditional_theorems.scope_limit: Coprimality is an additional hypothesis and is not assumed before the Lucas equation is proved.
unconditional_theorems.fixed_abscissa_correction: For an even number of pairwise coprime indices, adding the fixed x(P) makes the loss zero; no additional coordinate is required.

unconditional_theorems.scope: Finite triangular monic algebras over rational retained coordinates, with one guard, no other closed residuals, and geometrically reduced active fibers as stated in the theorem.
unconditional_theorems.coefficient_norm_bound: log2 ||F||_1 <= S*((beta+r)*C(n)+(r+1)*(2*n^3+4*n-2)) for n=2^r and the specified weighted operator norm bound 2^beta

unconditional_theorems.statement: For every number field K, O_K is Diophantine in K if and only if Z is Diophantine in K.
unconditional_theorems.published_input: Alpoge-Bhargava-Ho-Shnidman, Inventiones Mathematicae 243 (2026), Corollary 1.2: Z is Diophantine in O_K.
unconditional_theorems.conditional_addition: Assuming Z is Diophantine in Q, these assertions are equivalent to Q being Diophantine in K.
unconditional_theorems.coordinate_bound: A definition of Z in K with N total coordinates yields O_K with [K:Q]*N total coordinates.

unconditional_theorems.scope: Every finite extension L/K of characteristic-zero fields, with all witnesses in the ambient field L.
unconditional_theorems.equivalent_sets: K; relative norm image N_{L/K}(L); relative norm graph; relative trace graph are Diophantine in L simultaneously.
unconditional_theorems.coordinate_bound: M total coordinates for norm-image membership yield n*M total coordinates and n equations for K, where n=[L:K].
unconditional_theorems.proper_extension_obstruction: Norm and trace graphs are Zariski dense in the affine plane over L, so have no quantifier-free definitions.

unconditional_theorems.descent: An N-coordinate definition of O_L in L descends along a degree-d extension L/K to a definition of O_K in K with 1+d*(N-1) total coordinates, d equations, and unchanged degree bound.
unconditional_theorems.counterexample_consequence: An actual counterexample persists in every finite extension and yields a totally imaginary Galois counterexample.
unconditional_theorems.finite_collection_obstruction: Any fixed finite collection of existential formulas with infinite input projections over a number field simultaneously accepts some rational noninteger in a finite Galois extension of bounded degree.
unconditional_theorems.scope_limit: No actual counterexample to a separately chosen defining polynomial for each field is established.

unconditional_theorems.general_statement: For y^2=x^3+A*x+B over Q, if A,B are p-integral and B is a nonzero nonsquare modulo an odd prime p, every rational abscissa has even p-adic valuation.
unconditional_theorems.example: E:y^2=x^3-2 has the infinite-order point (3,5), but 5 is not in the multiplicative subgroup generated by its rational abscissas.
unconditional_theorems.scope_limit: This does not obstruct sums, more elaborate definitions, or definability of a ring of integers in its field.

unconditional_theorems.statement: No q in Z[X] of degree at most two simultaneously reflects rational integrality, is odd at every integer, and has r(q(x)) square in Q_2 at every integer.
unconditional_theorems.quadratic_classification: A*X^2+B*X+C with A nonzero reflects integrality if and only if |A| is squarefree and A divides B.
unconditional_theorems.scope_limit: Only this odd-valued, uncorrected contact-square normalization; not corrected or parity-free routes and not a lower bound for arbitrary defining polynomials.

unconditional_theorems.statement: In every listedQ(sqrt(d)), the projection is the same proper subsetD ofQ containing0,1 and excluding-1.
unconditional_theorems.local_statement: D is simultaneously dense in every finite product ofQ-completions; every local input has witnesses in every completion of each listed quadratic field.
unconditional_theorems.rank_verification: UnconditionalPARI ellrank bounds, with torsion and exact point calculations.
unconditional_theorems.scope_limit: Not a definition ofZ,Q,or a ring of integers, and not a counterexample to existence of a different definition.

unconditional_theorems.statement: IfS is Diophantine inK, Z is contained inS andM*S is contained inO_K for a fixed positive integerM, thenO_K is Diophantine inK.
unconditional_theorems.coordinate_bound: IfS usesN total coordinates, [K:Q]*N coordinates suffice.
unconditional_theorems.degree_bound: With one defining equation of degreed forS, [K:Q] equations of degree at mostM*d suffice.

unconditional_theorems.statement: A fixed polynomial denominator and a square resultant multiplier give 0<R_min<R_L(X)<1 for all real X and odd L>=3, with R_min and exceptional primes independent of L.
unconditional_theorems.integer_input_properties: Square reduced denominator, squares in Q_2,Q_3,Q_17, and prescribed positive local depths.
unconditional_theorems.scope_limit: No variable reduction or replacement of the finite reduction-order requirements is asserted.

unconditional_theorems.finite_presentation_bound: Recovering arbitrary tuples of r independent points in the specified simple Weil restriction by finite algebraic choices requires at least2r retained rational coordinates.
unconditional_theorems.index_graph: For a Zariski-dense cyclic subgroup of an abelian variety, the graph {(n,[n]P)} is Zariski dense in G_a times that variety.
unconditional_theorems.rational_curve_obstruction: The paired formal requirements H=[h]P at one split place and H-P at the other cannot hold for arbitrarily many good primes when E and P are rational.
unconditional_theorems.two_curve_scope: A curve correspondence containing a common-index graph yields an isogeny and prevents infinitely many coprime reduction orders.
unconditional_theorems.scope_limit: Restrictions on these specified compression mechanisms, not universal lower bounds for integer-defining polynomials.

large_prime_parity_counterexample.scope: These congruences alone; the full Gaussian-generator and avoidance conditions are not asserted.

unconditional_theorems.statement: Every finite union of fixed rational-function images on finite products of fixed abelian varieties over a number field, even with finitely many values added, misses infinitely many rational integers.
unconditional_theorems.source: Corvaja and Zannier, arXiv:2608.28255v1, Theorem1.1; Mordell-Weil finite generation.
unconditional_theorems.consequence: Finite rational operations on the specified stable-elliptic subsets cannot produce a set containing every integer.
unconditional_theorems.scope_limit: Does not cover arbitrary algebraic correspondences or unrestricted affine witnesses. Not a nondefinability theorem for rings of integers.

unconditional_theorems.statement: The projection in each specified quadratic field is zero together with ratios of nonzero rational elliptic slopes; it misses infinitely many rational integers.
unconditional_theorems.scope_limit: Not a definition of the rational subfield or a ring of integers. The bounded search does not certify particular omitted values.

unconditional_theorems.scope: Finite algebra B defined by independent scalar monic separable equations, extended by square roots; guard g times the product of the square-root generators with g in B.
unconditional_theorems.statement: The displayed finite integer polynomial preserves exactly the guarded rational base projection, including inactive nilpotents and disappearing branches.
For a variety mapping to an abelian variety, if each geometric fiber has only finitely many output values, its rational outputs meet every finitely generated multiplicative subgroup in a finite set.
unconditional_theorems.includes: Quasi-finite covers and affine translates of multiplicative subgroups; generic finiteness alone requires exceptional fibers to be treated separately.

unconditional_theorems.statement: Over an abelian base, bounded-denominator outputs with soluble unirational fibers or smooth proper genus-one fibers equipped with an ample line bundle cannot cover all integers.
genus_one_inputs: finite map to the relative Jacobian
unconditional_theorems.scope_limit: No obstruction for all higher-genus families, and no counterexample to general ring-of-integers definability.

unconditional_theorems.statement: No fixed rational value of the parameter e gives the complete stated zero-preparation pole certificate.
unconditional_theorems.scope_limit: These counterexamples range over prepared inputs. They do not exclude a fixed retained parameter on a specially selected prime-pattern subfamily.
unconditional_theorems.dense_prepared_counterexamples: For tau=+/-17, counterexamples are dense in every real subinterval of (0,17), with valuations4,2,2 at2,3,17.

unconditional_theorems.statement: Two explicit prepared inputs cannot share an actual pole parameter; symmetric contact products can have odd radical one at unbounded scale height.
unconditional_theorems.scope_limit: Obstructions to specified simplifications, not general coordinate lower bounds.

unconditional_theorems.statement: The natural even-power Frey family has exponential growth of the reduced j denominator in logarithmic height. Infinitely many required integer witnesses fail the fixed asymmetric-size hypotheses.
unconditional_theorems.frey_denominator_lower_bound: max(|A|,|B|)^(4*d)/256 for coprime nonzero A,B and positive even d
unconditional_theorems.scope_limit: Applicability obstruction for the specified families; neither disproves abc nor excludes other families.

unconditional_theorems.statement: For a Belyi map of degree d from a curve of genus g, hF(J)<=logNormDisc(C)/(2[K:Q])+g*log(2/sqrt(pi)), where C is the split order at the fibre t=2.
unconditional_theorems.finite_bad_prime_version: hF(J)<=d/2*(log2+lograd(S)+omega(S)*logd)+g*log(2/sqrt(pi)) when the normalization is finite etale away from S and0,1,infinity.
unconditional_theorems.modular_version: For X_H=X1(N)/H with -1 inH, S is the set of primes dividing6N and d=N*[(Z/NZ)^*:H]*product(p|N)(1+1/p).

unconditional_theorems.statement: Over any characteristic-zero field, three quadrics in S,T,f,g describe exactly H and H-P with finite nonzero abscissas, assuming abD(D^2+6a^2D-3a^4) is nonzero. All leading-coefficient exceptions are included.

Psi_z(D)=zD^2/(1+zD^2) has nonnegative valuation at every odd-valuation coefficient, uniformly over arbitrarily deep poles D. A unit coefficient detects positive valuation of D. Mixed even-valuation extraction and disjoint balanced contacts are proved.

For every rational a>4, lambda=-(a+1)/(5a) gives a negative nonzero square R(lambda)R(a*lambda), hence odd radical one. This applies to the source scales a=beta^8+T(n)^8. Positive unbounded-scale examples and the full twelve-element contact automorphism group are also proved.
unconditional_theorems.scope_limit: The fixed product alone cannot support a uniform height bound. These examples do not satisfy all the other elliptic and pole constraints automatically; no counterexample to the 13-variable theorem is claimed.

unconditional_theorems.scope: For every number field K with i not in K and every D in K*, with E_D:y^2=x^3-D*x and L=K(i).
unconditional_theorems.trace_statement: For a nontorsion P in E_D(K), C=(1+iota)P has Tr_L/K x([n]C)=Tr_L/Q x([n]C)=0 for all nonzero n, while h(x([n]C))=4*n^2*hat_h(P)+O_E(1).
unconditional_theorems.sum_statement: The four distinct doubled points [2n]P, iota[2n]P, [4n]P, iota[4n]P have distinct abscissas summing to zero and unbounded heights.
unconditional_theorems.explicit_nontorsion_certificate: Reduction orders5 and3 at primes17 and23; group orders20 and24 exclude torsion.
unconditional_theorems.scope_limit: An obstruction to extending the particular elliptic group and height mechanism; no counterexample to Diophantine definability of O_L in L is claimed.

unconditional_theorems.fixed_parameters: Odd integer B>=3, nonzero integer n, rational T>6; beta(X)=2*X^2+B; a(X)=beta(X)^8+T^8.
unconditional_theorems.statement: For every nonzero Psi in Q(X,lambda), there are a fixed positive cone of contact depths, a nonzero parity class, and infinitely many good primes such that every positive depth pair in that cone and parity class is realized by half-integral X and lambda=s^2+t^2>1 with integers s,t. The two contact values have those depths, Psi is defined and nonzero with even valuation, and beta(X)-n is a p-unit.
unconditional_theorems.scope: No additional arithmetic conjecture; includes explicit rational dependence on the input and scale. The source specialization T=Tr(x([n]P)) is covered whenever T>6.
unconditional_theorems.computation_scope: Two exact illustrative examples, independently checked by BigInt integer arithmetic and Fraction rational arithmetic; the universal statement is a formal-series and prime-existence proof.
unconditional_theorems.scope_limit: An obstruction to one rational function uniformly detecting the union of two odd contact valuations; no false solution of the complete Diophantine source and no absolute variable-count lower bound are asserted.
unconditional_theorems.stronger_slope_restriction: The same conclusions hold with lambda=1+s^2 for a nonzero integer s; lambda-1 is an integer square.

unconditional_theorems.finiteness: At each fixed scale and finite prime set, only finitely many admissible rational slopes have equal odd contact sets.
unconditional_theorems.scope: Genus, finiteness and the inert-prime comparison obstruction are unconditional. The separately stated one-pole soundness implication retains weak abc and the original arithmetic premises; its converse is open. No new defining variable count.

unconditional_theorems.statement: If ZP is Zariski dense in an abelian variety A, the triples ([n]P,[h]P,[nh]P) are Zariski dense in A^3 for any infinite set of n and any infinite set of h for each n.
unconditional_theorems.elliptic_proof: An elementary intersection-degree argument using graphs of multiplication.
unconditional_theorems.general_proof: Mordell-Lang gives a density criterion in terms of finite unions of rational affine hyperplanes in the index lattice.
unconditional_theorems.consequence: No fixed algebraic correspondence with finite geometric fibers can recover the index product uniformly on those pairs; nonlinear polynomial index graphs satisfy the analogous obstruction.
unconditional_theorems.scope: No claim about arbitrary Diophantine definitions, additional free parameters, positive-dimensional fibers with finite rational point sets, or specially selected finite sets of auxiliary indices.

unconditional_theorems.statement: For the contacts {-1,0,2,3}, infinitely many rational t have unbounded logarithmic height and odd contact radical one outside {2,3,5}; the points can be chosen with 3<t<5.
unconditional_theorems.proof_method: Exact birational transformations and a Nagell-Lutz nontorsion certificate give infinitely many rational points; the twist and contact differences bound the odd prime support.
unconditional_theorems.scope: An obstruction to height bounds using this particular four-contact odd radical. It is not a nonintegral solution of a complete defining source, a counterexample to abc, or a variable-count lower bound.

auxiliary_arithmetic_theorems.hypothesis: For K=Q(sqrt(2)), E:y^2=x^3-(3-sqrt(2))^2*x and P=2*(1+sqrt(2),2*sqrt(2)), assume 2E(K)=ZP.
auxiliary_arithmetic_theorems.statement: x=h^2, j^2=h^4-(3-sqrt(2))^2, y=h*j describe exactly the nonzero points of ZP; no index parity restriction is needed.

auxiliary_arithmetic_theorems.hypothesis: The cited Sun v2 prime-pattern and weighted reduction-order estimates, with fixed congruence and avoidance data.
auxiliary_arithmetic_theorems.statement: A fixed cutoff followed by a sufficiently slow diagonal tau allows removal of w<X^alpha for 1/4<alpha<1/2, leaving admissible patterns with gaps larger than Hasse-sized errors.
auxiliary_arithmetic_theorems.novelty_scope: An explicit dependency derivation recording the separation argument already used upstream, not a new independent prime theorem.
auxiliary_arithmetic_theorems.primary_reference: Sun, arXiv:2610.20691v2, Propositions 5.1 and 6.2 and Section 6.1.

auxiliary_arithmetic_theorems.premise: The stated five-contact odd-radical height bound with exponent19.
auxiliary_arithmetic_theorems.statement: For5r disjoint translated contacts, h(t)<=C_r+H E_r^19 M_r(t)^(19/r).
auxiliary_arithmetic_theorems.scope_limit: Derived height and normalization theorem; its four-block specialization is implemented in the 267-variable family.

auxiliary_arithmetic_theorems.hypothesis: The retained simultaneous-twist and nonzero pole-realization premises.
auxiliary_arithmetic_theorems.statement: The source pole witnesses are Zariski dense in the indicated parameter space and avoid any finite collection of proper polynomial zero sets.
auxiliary_arithmetic_theorems.scope_limit: Does not prove simultaneous rational solubility with a common retained pole parameter.

auxiliary_arithmetic_theorems.statement: Ordinary Szpiro supplies weak abc at exponent121/100, sufficient for the sixth-power thirteen-coordinate construction. Truncated Vojta implies ordinary abc, which supplies both leading thirteen-coordinate constructions. Pell examples show why consecutive-integer prime assignments alone do not control the odd radical.
auxiliary_arithmetic_theorems.other_conjectures: No coordinate reduction is derived from RH, GRH, or Grimm alone. No formal nonimplication is claimed.

auxiliary_arithmetic_theorems.premise: The modular realization in the inherited arithmetic construction, stated completely in the paper.
auxiliary_arithmetic_theorems.torsion_different_bound: The trace dual of the finite flat lci torsion order E[N] is N^(-1) times that order. Normalization and the tower formula give the modular vertical discriminant bound.

auxiliary_arithmetic_theorems.statement: The odd-valuation implication holds for y^2=T^2+kappa*R*(1+R*s^2)^2. For every m>=1, the prepared b_m=409*(204/1013^m)^2 gives no Q_1013-point on Y^2=1+b_m*(1+b_m*v^2)^2, including on its smooth projective model.
auxiliary_arithmetic_theorems.scope_limit: This disproves completeness on all prepared inputs even for a finite disjunction of fixed nonzero kappa values; the restricted comparison-prime family remains unresolved. No variable-count improvement follows.
auxiliary_arithmetic_theorems.general_obstruction: For every finite fixed set C of nonzero rational kappa, infinitely many prepared b tending to zero make all the corresponding smooth quartic curves locally insoluble at one prime.

auxiliary_arithmetic_theorems.premise: Full normalized source modular realization, including the quaternionic surface, its endomorphisms, and the repeated two-dimensional representation.
auxiliary_arithmetic_theorems.statement: h(a)<=C2*M5(a)^2*(1+log M5(a))^2 with explicit C2<2^221231; consequently h(a)<2^221234*M5(a)^(7/3). For every positive eta an effective exponent2+eta holds without restrictions on contact-prime character orders.
auxiliary_arithmetic_theorems.multiplicity_bound: If s is the nebentypus order and A_f is geometrically isogenous to A^r, then s/r<=4.
auxiliary_arithmetic_theorems.height_transfer: Rémond height superadditivity gives a surface factor of height at most h(J_H)/r, followed by a dimension-two explicit isogeny estimate.
auxiliary_arithmetic_theorems.scope_limit: This is a consequence of the full stated modular realization, not a theorem from the conductor inequality alone.

auxiliary_arithmetic_theorems.unconditional_height_lemma: For integers r>=1 and B>=1, if gamma>=1 or r is even, beta=gamma^r+B satisfies beta>=B and r*h(gamma)<=h(beta), uniformly in B.
auxiliary_arithmetic_theorems.scope: These are height-transfer criteria. The five-contact criterion alone supplies no new defining polynomial or coordinate count; the complete six-contact construction is proved separately.

additional_hypothesis_constructions.zero_input_branch: The final polynomial F_B=X*Q_B adds input zero; all nonzero integer indices, including negative and even indices, have complete guarded-source witnesses.
additional_hypothesis_constructions.scope_limit: Thirteen total coordinates under an additional arithmetic hypothesis; this degree improvement does not reduce the established coordinate count. The numeric fixture has no certified defining threshold.
additional_hypothesis_constructions.general_height_theorem: For every one weak abc exponent 1<kappa<4/3, any even d with (8/kappa-6)*(d/kappa-3)>1 gives the same thirteen-coordinate construction after a sufficiently large fixed odd shift.

additional_hypothesis_constructions.role: Leading quartic under ordinary rational abc.
additional_hypothesis_constructions.ordinary_monomial_count_condition: Every positive coefficient parameter; this is separate from the defining threshold.
additional_hypothesis_constructions.common_elliptic_chart: Three quadrics in four field coordinates; all exceptional strata proved.
additional_hypothesis_constructions.factor_clearing: Store A_i=s*T_i, (R+1)*Omega=A_1*A_2, and the scaled trace eta; s3*b=eta^2 is exactly the new-contact pole input.
